text.p: SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Jan Slota, chairman of the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said the time was now ripe for an early election. Slota was reacting to Tuesday's vote of another junior coalition member, the Workers Party (ZRS), against the controversial amendment to the penal code, initiated by SNS.
PRAVDA - The Slovak parliament on Tuesday added a proposal to postpone privatisation of financial institutions to the agenda of its February session.
- The parliament failed to approve members of the newly- created committees supervising the state secret service and the military secret service.

NARODNA OBRODA - Only 3,736 privatisation bonds have changed hands in anonymous trading on the RM-System since the beginning of trading last August. The market now registers more than 340,000 orders to sell the bonds. Some 30,708 bonds were sold in direct trades.
- Swedish forestry company AssiDoman AB said it planned to acquire 100 percent in the Slovak paper and paperboard company JCP Sturovo. AssiDoman already holds about 90-percent of JCP.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - State-controlled heavy engineering company ZTS TEES martin said its production was expected to total some 4.9 billion crowns in 1997, with sales reaching about five billion.
- ZTS TEES said it planned to invest about 300 million crowns for modernisation programmes this year.
PRACA - The paper quotes unnamed sources as saying that South Korea's Samsung is considering selling its stake in a refrigerator producing joint-venture with Slovak white goods producer Calex.
- The Slovak government wants to participate in repaying the debts of the troubled Calex a.s., totalling some eight billion crowns.
